headline: President Signs Sweeping Civil Rights Bill Into Law
dispatch: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act into law at the White House on July 2, 1964, with more than 70 pens used to complete the signing, distributed afterward as keepsakes. The act bans discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin in schools, workplaces, and public accommodations. It is the most far-reaching civil rights legislation passed by Congress since Reconstruction.
answer: President Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act, 1964
